title: Incomplete Open Tesseracts: How Many Connected Edge Shapes Does the 4-Cube Have, and Does LeWitt's Rule Still Count 122 in 3D?
target_platform: C (cc -O2, pthreads) exact Burnside enumeration plus standard-library Python independent checker; no network, no paid inference during the experiment
interest_statement: Richard invoked the associative-mission-discovery prompt (own-choice, one mission). Four domains were chosen deliberately (not randomly): change ringing, periodical cicadas, Sol LeWitt's wall drawings and incomplete open cubes, and the Venetian doge election. The crossing that held my interest: the 24 rotations of a cube are in bijection with the 24 rows of a four-bell extent (rotation group = S4 acting on the four body diagonals), so ringing four bells is a tour of every cube orientation by edge half-turns. That made me ask what LeWitt's 'incomplete open' rule counts one dimension up, where the analogy visibly breaks (the 4-cube rotation group has order 192, not 120 = |S5|). The association is generative provenance; it is not what is tested. Prior-work check found LeWitt's 122 already verified (Rozhkovskaya 2014; Pitt; Weychert; Vejdemo-Johansson 2026 for Platonic solids) and no enumeration for the tesseract in the sources inspected, so the 3D count is a validity gate and the 4D count is the new-here contribution (a distinct framing relative to sources inspected, not an exhaustive novelty claim).
hypothesis: Let Q_n be the n-cube graph, S_n the non-empty, non-complete, connected edge subsets, and k(S) the number of axis directions in which S has an edge. Orbits are counted by exact Burnside enumeration over the rotation group (det +1 signed permutations, order 24 for n=3, 192 for n=4) and over all symmetries (48, 384). (G, development) The engine gives 122 rotation orbits at n=3, k=3 (LeWitt's count) and 77 under all symmetries, both equal to an independent brute-force canonical-form count. (H1, held-out n=4) Instrument consistency: every Burnside sum is divisible by its group order; identity counts depend only on k; the engine's fixed-set counts equal an independent Python brute count for every group element with at most 12 edge cycles (308 elements); and C and Python agree on all 300,034 development masks. (H2, held-out n=4 forecast) The number of rotation orbits with k=4 lies in [14,400,000, 14,800,000] (forecast frozen after dev sampling gave a connected fraction of 0.6523 +- 0.0009, so identity count about 2.80e9). (H3) Chirality is real in 4D: the all-symmetry k=4 count is strictly between half and all of the rotation k=4 count.
falsification_criteria: UNASSESSED (verdict null) if the gate G fails, any H1 check fails or cannot be run, the run exceeds its resource ceiling, or output is incomplete: instrument failure is not a finding. FALSIFIED if H1 holds and H2 or H3 fails (the instrument is validated but the forecast or chirality claim is wrong); the measured count is then reported as the result. CORROBORATED only if G, H1, H2 and H3 all hold. Whatever the verdict, the exact Q4 counts by k for both groups are recorded. Claims are limited to these definitions (connected, incomplete, k axes, proper rotations count mirror images as distinct) on the 3-cube and 4-cube; exhaustive finite computation establishes that finite result only. The cicada/ringing/Venice crossings are untested provenance.
baseline_evidence: LeWitt 1974 lists 122 incomplete open cubes (connected, non-planar edge subsets, rotation equivalence, mirror images distinct); Rozhkovskaya (Nexus Network Journal 2014) and Pitt's brute-force re-derivation confirm 122; Weychert's 4,094 is 2^12-2 before filters; Vejdemo-Johansson arXiv 2602.20425 reports orbit counts for the five Platonic solids (6, 122, 185, 2,423,206, 16,096,166) and does not cover the tesseract. 'Surfaces in the Tesseract' (arXiv 2311.06596) studies closed face-surfaces, a different object. Inspected: abstracts, search summaries and Pitt's post; full papers not read. No Q4 edge-subset count has been run by this mission before freezing.
experiment: Phase 1 elaboration/research (done: discovery.md). Phase 2 development: build burnside.c, aggregate.py, independent.py; validate on n=3 and on Q4 masks and cheap group elements (no held-out count). Phase 3: commit protocol.md, freeze.json with SHA-256 of code, dev outputs and forecast before any Q4 full enumeration. Phase 4: run burnside 4 (2^32 identity enumeration plus 383 smaller elements) on 8 threads, aggregate, compare with the Python fixed-set counts. Phase 5: assess, one bounded OpenRouter cross-family review of protocol and code (cost-capped), reflection, closeout. Side artifact (exploratory, unfrozen): ringing_the_cube.md, a verified 24-row plain-changes tour of the cube rotations.
score_basis: Planning estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 1: curiosity-driven, little direct project utility. Depth 3: exact enumeration with an independently validated instrument and a forecast that can fail, but a known method on a new object. Cost 0.1 and friction 2: minutes of local CPU; risk is definition ambiguity (non-planar generalised to 4D) and instrument bugs, handled by reporting every k.
